description: UI + App wiring for B3 durability: port the restore dialogs with this app's a11y convention, add the restore-on-launch host, add the Settings auto-backup card (toggle + download full backup + restore-from-auto-backup list + backup reminder), start the snapshot controller in App after the manager loads, and refresh the manager after any restore. DEPENDS ON FEAT-001 (consumes snapshot-store/-service/-settings, restore-service, backup-service/reminder). Independent of FEAT-001 only in that it adds no new storage logic — it must run AFTER FEAT-001.
steps: Port d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\components\shared\RestoreConfirmDialog.tsx (+ RestoreConfirmDialog.module.css ported from the WFRP CSS) — the confirm dialog showing character count, a names list (truncated at 50), and a duplicate-will-be-copied warning. Use this app's dialog a11y convention like ConfirmDialog.tsx: wrap with useFocusTrap + useBodyScrollLock, Escape cancels, role=dialog + aria-modal, overlay-click cancels.

Port d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\components\shared\RestoreLaunchDialog.tsx — the discrepancy prompt ('A more recent backup from <time> was found — restore it?') with Restore / Not now actions. Reuse RestoreConfirmDialog.module.css. Apply the same a11y (focus trap or the dialog's existing manual trap, Escape declines, aria-modal, labelled heading). It NEVER auto-acts.

Create d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\components\shared\RestoreLaunchHost.tsx: a run-once mount check gated by isAutoBackupEnabled(); call getSnapshotStore() then evaluateLaunchDiscrepancy; render RestoreLaunchDialog ONLY on a genuine discrepancy; on Restore route through restoreFromSnapshot -> RestoreConfirmDialog -> commitSnapshotRestore -> call props.onRestored(); on Decline clear state and leave snapshots intact. Set-state happens inside the async callback (not synchronously in the effect body). Props: { onRestored: () => void }.

Create d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\components\settings\AutoBackupCard.tsx (+ AutoBackupCard.module.css) following the ExportImportCard.tsx pattern (Card + SectionHeader + lucide icons + transient status): an auto-backup toggle bound to isAutoBackupEnabled/setAutoBackupEnabled; a 'Download full backup' button (assembleBackup -> downloadBackup over ALL characters, with a count/skipped message); a 'Restore from auto-backup' affordance that lists snapshots by timestamp (getSnapshotStore().listSnapshots()), and on choosing one routes through restoreFromSnapshot -> a confirm (RestoreConfirmDialog or ConfirmDialog) -> commitSnapshotRestore -> props.onRestored(); and the backup reminder text (getLastBackupAt + getBackupReminder -> 'Last backed up N days ago' / 'never'). Props: { onRestored: () => void }.

Thread the card into d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\components\pages\SettingsPage.tsx: render <AutoBackupCard onRestored={...} /> below the existing <ExportImportCard/>. Add an `onRestored` (manager-refresh) prop to SettingsPageProps and pass it through from App.

Add a reload path to d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\hooks\useCharacterManager.ts: expose `reload: () => Promise<void>` on UseCharacterManagerResult that re-runs resolveActiveCharacter + listSummaries and re-sets characters/activeId/activeCharacter/status (extract the existing initial-load effect body into a callable so both the mount effect and reload share it).

Wire d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\App.tsx: (a) after the manager settles (status 'ready' or 'welcome'), in an effect, call getSnapshotStore().init() then startSnapshotController(getSnapshotStore()) once, and stop() it on unmount; (b) fire notifyCharacterDataChange() on the live save path — call it right after the saveCharacter(...) in handleChange so the controller sees the change; (c) mount <RestoreLaunchHost onRestored={reload} /> around the normal shell so it can prompt only on discrepancy and refresh the manager after a restore; (d) pass onRestored={reload} down to SettingsPage. Do NOT change the welcome/ready/error branches' existing behaviour.

Create d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\components\shared\__tests__\RestoreLaunchHost.test.tsx and d:\Git\DNDCharSheet\src\components\settings\__tests__\AutoBackupCard.test.tsx (adapt the WFRP snapshot-restore.integration.test.tsx where it transfers): RestoreLaunchHost prompts ONLY on a discrepancy (no dialog when live is a superset of the latest snapshot; a dialog when live is empty but a snapshot exists) and routes a confirmed restore through the service; AutoBackupCard renders, the toggle persists via snapshot-settings, 'Download full backup' calls the backup path, and the restore list routes a chosen snapshot through restoreFromSnapshot/commitSnapshotRestore and calls onRestored.
acceptance_criteria: The restore-on-launch host shows a prompt ONLY when detectDiscrepancy flags a genuine discrepancy (live empty/missing-ids vs the latest snapshot) and never auto-overwrites — every restore goes through restore-service's validate + adopt-as-new path.

SettingsPage renders the auto-backup toggle, a 'Download full backup' button (all characters), a 'Restore from auto-backup' list by timestamp, and the backup reminder; the toggle state persists across reloads via snapshot-settings.

App starts startSnapshotController after the manager loads, fires the character-data change signal on the live save path, mounts RestoreLaunchHost, and refreshes the manager (list + active character) after any restore.
The restore dialogs use the app's a11y convention (focus trap, body-scroll-lock, Escape, aria-modal).
findings:
UI + App wiring for B3 durability implemented and verified. Exit gate all green: `npx vitest run src/components` = 34 files / 473 tests pass; `npm run typecheck` clean; `npx eslint .` 0 errors/0 warnings; `npm test` = 103 files / 2476 tests pass; `npm run build` succeeds and emits dist/sw.js.

WHAT WAS BUILT:
- src/components/shared/RestoreConfirmDialog.tsx (+ .module.css): confirm dialog (character count, names list truncated at 50, duplicate-will-be-copied warning). Uses the app's a11y convention (useFocusTrap + useBodyScrollLock + Escape + role=dialog/aria-modal/aria-labelledby + overlay-click cancel) — the WFRP source had none; hardened to match ConfirmDialog.tsx.
- src/components/shared/RestoreLaunchDialog.tsx: the discrepancy prompt ('A more recent backup from <time> was found — restore it?') with Restore / Not now. Reuses RestoreConfirmDialog.module.css and the SAME a11y convention (Escape declines, aria-modal, labelled heading). Never auto-acts.
- src/components/shared/RestoreLaunchHost.tsx: run-once mount check gated by isAutoBackupEnabled(); getSnapshotStore()+evaluateLaunchDiscrepancy; renders RestoreLaunchDialog ONLY on a genuine discrepancy; Restore -> restoreFromSnapshot -> RestoreConfirmDialog -> commitSnapshotRestore -> props.onRestored(); Decline clears state. Set-state only inside the async callback. Props { onRestored }.
- src/components/settings/AutoBackupCard.tsx (+ .module.css): ExportImportCard-pattern card (Card + SectionHeader + lucide icons Save/Download/History/RotateCcw + transient status). Toggle bound to isAutoBackupEnabled/setAutoBackupEnabled; 'Download full backup' (assembleBackup -> downloadBackup over ALL characters, with a count message); 'Restore from auto-backup' lists snapshots by timestamp (getSnapshotStore().listSnapshots()) and routes a chosen snapshot through restoreFromSnapshot -> RestoreConfirmDialog -> commitSnapshotRestore -> onRestored(); backup reminder text (getLastBackupAt + getBackupReminder -> 'Last backed up N days ago' / 'never'). Props { onRestored }.
- SettingsPage.tsx: added required `onRestored` to SettingsPageProps and renders <AutoBackupCard onRestored={...}/> below <ExportImportCard/>.
- useCharacterManager.ts: extracted the initial-load effect body into a shared `runLoad(isCancelled?)` callback; mount effect calls it inside an async IIFE (keeps setState after an await to satisfy react-hooks/set-state-in-effect); added `reload(): Promise<void>` to UseCharacterManagerResult.
- App.tsx: (a) after the manager settles (status 'ready'|'welcome'), an effect calls getSnapshotStore().init() then startSnapshotController(store) once and stop()s on unmount (isolated/non-fatal); (b) fires notifyCharacterDataChange() on the live save path — in handleChange after saveCharacter(...) resolves (so a snapshot never captures an unsaved edit); (c) mounts <RestoreLaunchHost onRestored={()=>void reload()} /> gated by managerSettled && !showWelcome; (d) passes onRestored={()=>void reload()} to SettingsPage. Welcome/ready/error branches unchanged.
- Tests: src/components/shared/__tests__/RestoreLaunchHost.test.tsx (no prompt when live ⊇ latest snapshot; prompt when live empty + snapshot exists; a confirmed restore routes through restoreCharacters non-destructively and calls onRestored) and src/components/settings/__tests__/AutoBackupCard.test.tsx (renders; toggle persists via snapshot-settings; Download full backup calls assembleBackup+downloadBackup; restore list routes a chosen snapshot through restoreCharacters and calls onRestored). Both use fake-indexeddb with the _reset*ForTests() + deleteDatabase beforeEach idiom and vi.spyOn(URL,'createObjectURL').

FINDINGS / NOTES:
1. TEST SEEDING: character-store.saveCharacter does NOT mint an id (only createCharacter does), and BLANK_CHARACTER.id === '' — detectDiscrepancy ignores blank snapshot ids, so seeding a character with id '' makes evaluateLaunchDiscrepancy return null. Tests therefore seed via the store's createCharacter(name) (real id) then adoptCharacter. The live app is unaffected (its creation flows all build on createCharacter).
2. backup-service BackupResult only carries `skipped` on the `ok:false` branch, so the AutoBackupCard success message reports the saved count only (no skipped count on success) — a skipped-count line would not type-check.
3. Fixed two pre-existing SettingsPage tests (SettingsPage.test.tsx, SettingsPage.dice.test.tsx) that broke when `onRestored` became a required prop — added onRestored={vi.fn()} to their render calls (fix-errors rule; smallest change).
4. Steering: B3 is durability infra with NO game mechanics — each new file carries a one-line 'no rulebook citation applies' note; no suppressions (@ts-ignore/eslint-disable/test-skips) were added; the set-state-in-effect lint error was fixed at the root (async IIFE) rather than suppressed.
